title: Uncurried finite projections of the enriched sequence adjunction
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], exact evaluations $e_n$ [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], derived tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and derived internal Hom $H$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $p:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ have inverse image on underlying sheaves the constant sequence, with ring map given by $A\to B_n$. Write $\mathcal R=Lp^*$ and $\mathcal L=R\lim\,U$ with the projection-normalized adjunction [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections]. For $P\in D(A)$ and $N\in D(\mathscr S(B))$ with both $\mathcal R P$ and $N$ normalized (each transition-adjoint map $M_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n\to M_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\ge n$), put $V=H_A(P,\mathcal L N)$ and $J=H_B(\mathcal R P,N)$. Define $b:\mathcal R V\to J$ as the transpose of reduced evaluation followed by the counit, and $\delta=\mathcal L(b)u_V:V\to\mathcal L J$ [lem-coef-closed-adjunction-enriched-isomorphism]. Identify $J_n=H_{B_n}(P\otimes_A^LB_n,N_n)$ by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The nth projection of $\delta$ is the unique $A$-linear map whose scalar-extension adjunct has closed transpose $$ (V\otimes_A^LB_n)\otimes^L_{B_n}(P\otimes_A^LB_n)\cong(V\otimes_A^LP)\otimes_A^LB_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}\otimes1}(\mathcal L N)\otimes_A^LB_n\xrightarrow{e_{N,n}}N_n.$$ Equivalently it is the internal scalar-extension adjunction applied after $H_A(P,\pi_n)$. After global sections and the specified comparison of [lem-coef-sequence-sections-limit-comparison], this is the global derived scalar-extension mapping-complex adjunction applied after $(\pi_n)_*$. On degree-zero Hom it sends $h:P\to\mathcal L N$ to $e_{N,n}\circ(h\otimes_A^LB_n)$.

proof.text: Naturality of π at the defining comparison b and the given unit normalization imply that the scalar adjunct of finiteProjection is ρ⁻¹ followed by evaluated b and homIdentification. The same argument applied to the system counit identifies the scalar adjunct of π_N with counitLevel. This is formal adjunction transposition and uses no faithfulness of evaluation.

Uncurry the defining enriched comparison using its evaluation construction. The tensorEvaluation and homEvaluation_evaluation equations transport evaluation to level n; naturality in the first Hom input inserts the inverse ρ on P. Inverting the supplied tensor compatibility equation identifies the resulting tensor map with ν⁻¹. Naturality of ρ then gives precisely reducedEvaluation.

The scalar adjunction Hom equivalence and the closed transpose are bijections. Their composite defining uncurried is injective, so finiteProjection is the unique map with the computed reduced evaluation.

Use the representing property of ClosedScalarHom.component to uncurry its inverse after H_A(P,π_N). Naturality of evaluation gives scalar(evaluation) followed by the scalar adjunct of π_N. The projected counit identity from step 1 identifies this with reducedEvaluation. Injectivity from step 3 proves finiteProjection = internalScalarMap.

Apply coefficientSequenceSectionsLimitComparison. Compare its derived pair with the supplied pair p using rightDerivedUnique and the universal unit equation. rightDerived_ext and the specified complex projection formulas identify the transported projections with πP. Whiskering this unique isomorphism transports κ and its unit normalization. Naturality of the scalar restriction comparison and the given π = hL followed by projection identify globalProjection with sections of finiteProjection followed by the inverse scalar comparison; substitute step 4.

Apply lem-coef-scalar-hom-zero-compatibility to the single map A→B_n with the given scalar data, closed representative models and the unit-normalized finite sections comparisons. The tensor equation identifies ν with evaluatedTensorComparison, so the supplied representative model applies to ν. The compatibility theorem computes the degree-zero image as the scalar adjunct of h followed by π_n. Adjunction naturality and the unit-normalized projection calculation identify this adjunct with scalar(h) followed by counitLevel.
